title: Pair Programming's Origins in Extreme Programming (1990s)
explainer: Pair programming as a formal practice grew out of Kent Beck's work on the Chrysler Comprehensive Compensation (C3) project in the mid-1990s and was codified as one of the core practices of Extreme Programming in his 1999 book. The practice framed continuous code review and knowledge transfer between two people, one typing, one watching and questioning, as a built-in mentorship loop rather than an occasional event, the same logic behind structured mentoring today.

title: Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development
explainer: In the early 1930s, psychologist Lev Vygotsky described a "zone of proximal development": the gap between what a learner can do alone and what they can do with help from a more knowledgeable other. Researchers who later built on his work used the term "scaffolding" for the support a mentor provides and gradually withdraws as the learner gains ability, which is essentially a formal description of what effective technical mentorship looks like in practice.
